title: Go SDK: response adapters and ergonomic stream + retry patterns
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: Several customers and internal examples use the Go SDK to consume streamed generation and structured outputs. Current helpers exist but are inconsistent: some callers must write manual json.RawMessage plumbing, others use non-generic typed helpers that duplicate code across models.

Goal: Deliver a small set of generic, composable response adapters that let callers: 1) decode streamed tokens into typed Go structs with minimal boilerplate; 2) use an ergonomic stream consumer API that supports backoff/retry hooks and graceful cancellation; 3) preserve backwards compatibility (existing blocking decode helpers should continue to work); and 4) ship examples and tests demonstrating common patterns (websocket consumer, server-sent events, file-backed retries).

Scope: Implement adapter primitives in the client package (no heavy runtime changes). Provide: DecodeAdapter[T any] that maps token/fragment events to T, StreamConsumer abstraction with Context cancellation + Done channel, and a RetryPolicy shape that is pluggable into both blocking and streaming paths. Update docs and add three example apps.
technical_notes: Design: introduce DecodeAdapter[T any] with a small interface: AcceptFragment([]byte) error, Result() (T, error). This keeps state internal and isolates JSON incremental decode concerns.
Streaming ergonomics: StreamConsumer provides Next() (fragment []byte, err error) and Close() error. Consumers can call Next in a goroutine and decode with DecodeAdapter concurrently.

Retries: define a RetryPolicy struct (MaxAttempts,int; Backoff func(attempt int) time.Duration; OnRetry func(ctx context.Context, meta map[string]string)). RetryPolicy will be a value type passed to both blocking Generate() and streaming StreamGenerate() helpers.

Backwards compatibility: export thin wrapper functions that implement the old helper names (DecodeToStructBlock, StreamToChan) but delegating to the new adapters. Keep deprecated comment tags for one release.

Performance: incremental decoding should avoid allocations where possible; use json.Decoder.Token when fragment boundaries are token aligned. For large JSON arrays we will decode into pointers and reuse them across iterations when safe.
Trade-offs: keeping the public API small favors fewer abstractions (Adapter + Consumer + RetryPolicy). More feature-rich retry DSL was considered but deferred to avoid API bloat.
acceptance_criteria: Provide DecodeAdapter[T any] implementation and unit tests that cover nested structs, optional fields, and streaming partial fragments.
Implement StreamConsumer abstraction and verify with integration tests against the hosted streaming playground endpoint.
RetryPolicy pluggable into Generate() and StreamGenerate() with deterministic unit tests (use fake clock/backoff).
No breaking changes to existing public functions; old helpers available with deprecation notices.
Documentation: README examples for blocking decode, streaming decode, and a practical retry example (exponential backoff with jitter).
Add three example programs in /examples/go: stream-to-file, serve-sse-with-decoder, and retrying-client-demo.
testing_plan: Unit tests for DecodeAdapter using crafted fragmented JSON byte slices (edge cases: partial UTF-8 rune, braces split across fragments).
Integration test that spins up the streaming test fixture (dockerized echo server) and asserts decoded typed results match expected sequence.
Fuzz test to ensure decoder doesn't panic on malformed fragments.
Benchmarks comparing adapter incremental decode vs full buffer unmarshal for common payload sizes (small: <1KB, medium: 10KB, large: 200KB).
Add CI job gating for examples that run against the public staging stream endpoint (uses test API key).
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind feature flag go.sdk.typed-adapters; opt-in by examples first.
Publish go-sdk-1.2.0-beta with changelog and migration notes. Request early adopters to test streaming workloads.
After 2 weeks of monitoring and zero regressions, flip default for new installations and deprecate old helpers in comments only.
Monitor telemetry: increased errors from streaming decode, retry count per-call, and average latency impact. Roll back if error rate spike > 3x baseline.
Coordinate with docs and release engineering for changelog and migration guide.
comments: 2026-02-21 Maya Thompson: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed to keep API minimal. Mentioned reuse of existing json.Decoder in adapter. Action: Arjun to prototype DecodeAdapter by 2026-02-27.

2026-02-28 Arjun Patel: Prototype complete. Found that json.Decoder.Token cannot handle our byte-fragment boundaries easily when braces split across fragments; implemented fragment buffer with incremental concatenation and a small state machine. Prototype in branch feat/decoder-adapter-31209.

2026-03-03 Review (Luis Chen): API looks good. Request: add explicit Close/Reset methods to adapters to allow reuse in long-running loop. Also add example showing streaming -> channel fan-out pattern.
2026-03-05 QA (Priya Singh): Added integration tests against staging streaming fixture. Discovered race in Cancel path (consumer goroutine leaked). Patch submitted in PR 4213, awaiting review.

2026-03-08 Arjun Patel: Addressed race by ensuring Close triggers consumer's context cancel and we wait on consumer done channel with 250ms timeout. Added unit test that forces Cancel during payload arrival.

2026-03-09 PM review (Ethan Wallace): Please add migration blurb for customers using older streaming helpers; note that behavior for malformed fragments is now deterministic (error on first malformed fragment).
